Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
Yes. ResStock’s **Geometry Wall Type data for Maine are incorrect** because of mislabeled county tax assessor data. For example, the 2024 Release 2 dataset represents Maine’s single-family detached homes as approximately 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete (CMU), which the team confirmed is inconsistent with Maine’s housing stock. The issue report says **no fix has been implemented** and all published ResStock datasets are believed to be affected. [ResStock issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The report recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use nearby states’ ResStock results, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For upgrade results that depend on wall type**, such as insulation measures restricted to wood-frame walls: either **reweight Maine results using nearby states’ wall type distributions**, or use nearby states’ results directly.

The full impacts remain under investigation, although the team currently does not expect significant effects on energy consumption, emissions, or energy bills. [Recommendations and impacts](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html#recommendation)
